pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP8, EP1, single HGX node (NVSwitch, world size 8). Engram tables (202.76 GB / 188.83 GiB) mandatorily offloaded to host RAM via --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'; TP4 is 8.88 GB/GPU short even with that. KV is REPLICATED on every rank (num_key_value_heads=1), so max_concurrency does not scale with n_gpus. 16/32 GPUs fit but cross InfiniBand for no gain; use DP2xTP8 replicas instead of TP16.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 experts dequant-to-BF16 (Marlin W4A16) — sm_90 has no FP4 tensor core, so 4-bit buys the 8x80 GB fit and zero FLOPS; non-expert FP8 32x32 UE8M0 runs with software block scaling. KV executes at BF16 3,200 B/token (not the advertised 890 B FP4 record, which needs nvfp4_ds_mla -> FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 -> sm_10x). VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT is arithmetically impossible at TP8 (+32.44 GiB/GPU needed, 32.74 GiB free). NVFP4 build is 17 GB larger for identical math — do not use.
pairs.attention_kernel: vLLM FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41, block size 64 on SM90 (gate: capability.major in [9,10]). FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (fused norm+RoPE+attn+RoPE+cast) and FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 are SM100+/SM12x only — losing the mega-attn fusion is a leading suspect for the 2.11x roofline gap. FlashMLA README says V4.1 sparse DECODE is SM100-only, conflicting with vLLM's gate and with working H100 runs (open question). FA2/FA3/FA4 do not apply: the operator is a gather-based sparse_attn over 640 entries with a learned sink. DSA indexer top-k via DeepGEMM FP8 MQA-logits + FlashInfer radix top-k.
pairs.headline: Runs today on 8xH100 (vLLM nightly, TP8, Engram on host) but at 89.8 out tok/s/GPU MEASURED — 12.9x slower than 2xB300. No FP4 tensor core: Marlin W4A16 + BF16 KV 3,200 B/tok, not 890. Measured cost $9.90-$21.28/1M output vs DeepSeek's own API at $0.60. Never beats the API on output.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 single HGX node (vLLM, what every measurement uses) or TP8+EP8 (SGLang, 15.7x slower measured). TP4 only with --engram-config cpu_offload: vLLM's shipped TP4 H200 profile is 1.07 GB/GPU over budget before any KV. MQA (1 KV head) means the compressed KV latent + indexer K replicate on every TP rank; routers, mHC F32 coefficients and norms (~0.40 GB) also replicate. No multi-node below 16 GPUs; Hopper's largest NVLink domain is 8.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 experts dequant-to-BF16 (Marlin W4A16 / FlashInfer SM90 CUTLASS) — memory win kept, compute win lost, expert GEMMs run at the 989.5 TFLOPS BF16 rate; non-expert FP8 32x32 UE8M0 native. KV executes FP8 (~1,650 B/token), NOT the checkpoint's 890 B FP4 cache (nvfp4_ds_mla needs FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41, major==10 only). Optional W4A8 via --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 and FP8 re-encode via VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1 are both V4-only evidence.
pairs.attention_kernel: vLLM FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (gate capability.major in [9,10], block size 64 on SM90, head size 512) + DeepseekV41IndexerBackend + sparse-SWA backend. FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (fused norm-RoPE-attn-RoPE-cast, and the only route to the FP4 KV cache) is SM100-only. FlashInfer sparse MLA for V4.1 is major in [10,12]. FA2/FA3/FA4 do not support this gather-based sparse_attn operator on any GPU. FlashMLA's README says V4.1 sparse decode is SM100-only, but vLLM ships its own sm_90 instantiation and InferenceX has 8 measured H200 points plus GSM8K 0.971-0.975 from it.
pairs.headline: Runs today on 8xH200 TP8 (vLLM nightly), Engram resident, GSM8K 0.971-0.975 — but as MXFP4-dequant-to-BF16 with FP8 KV (1,650 B/tok, not 890), and 3.6x slower per GPU than B200 on the identical InferenceX trace. Self-hosting loses to DeepSeek's own $0.60/M API at any interactive utilisation.

contradictions: gpus/h200.md §2's own DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash worked table (EP8, N=8) gives max concurrency 46,153/14,673/3,935 (FP4 KV) and 28,654/8,259/2,146 (FP8 KV) at 8K/32K/128K context. models/deepseek41f/h200.md §1.2-§1.3's aggregate reading for the identical N=8 EP8 configuration gives 45,832/14,572/3,908 (FP4) and 28,457/8,202/2,132 (FP8) -- consistently ~0.7% lower at every cell. Root cause: gpus/h200.md's node-KV-budget formula (141e9*0.9*8 - 510.29e9 - 8*4GiB = 470.55 GB) omits the ~0.40 GB/GPU of replicated non-shardable tensors (ffn.gate routers, mHC coefficients, KV compressors) that models/deepseek41f/h200.md's own §1.3 tensor-sharding analysis derives and subtracts (giving 467.4 GB). Both documents are internally consistent with the formula each states; this is an unresolved granularity mismatch between the two documents, not fixed in either (both under the 5% threshold), flagged per instructions rather than silently picked.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B200 (HGX 8-GPU, sm_100, 180 GB)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 single node (8-GPU NVLink island), optionally +EP8 via --enable-expert-parallel; vLLM's own B200 recipe is TP4. KV cache is REPLICATED on every TP rank (MLA latent, num_key_value_heads=1) — measured via InferenceX kv_cache_pool_tokens; DP-attention/DCP unverified for this model on B200. TP>8 crosses the 0.8 TB/s node fabric (36x cliff) — wide-EP is a GB200/GB300 NVL72 play, not HGX B200.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native, executed as W4A8 (MXFP4 E2M1/E8M0-per-32 weights x MXFP8 activations) — runs on Blackwell's FP8 line (4,500 TFLOPS dense), NOT the 9,000 TFLOPS FP4 line; non-expert tensors FP8 E4M3 on 32x32 UE8M0 tiles; embeddings/lm_head/vision BF16. No dequant or requant anywhere in the B200 path.
pairs.attention_kernel: FlashMLA sparse decode DSV4.1 (SM100-exclusive) via FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41, or FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 with nvfp4_ds_mla FP4 KV (SM100 only, block 128), or FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41; SGLang defaults to trtllm_mla (1.2x prefill / 1.45x decode vs FlashMLA on B200). No FlashAttention path — vLLM refuses FA3 on Blackwell and FA4 has no CSA2 operator. DSA/CSA2 indexer top-k via FlashInfer top_k_varlen radix kernel / SGLang Lightning TopK.
pairs.headline: Runs natively on B200 today (vLLM nightly, "b200: verified"); min TP4, best TP8. MXFP4 executes W4A8 on the FP8 line, not FP4. $0.46-1.08/1M output interactive. B200 matches B300 within 2.5% until its 180 GB KV pool runs out at concurrency 128, then collapses (TTFT 48 s vs 0.50 s).

contradictions: B200 usable capacity: METHODOLOGY §8 and gpus/b200.md §2 pin 180 GB as-deployed (used throughout this document's §1.2/§1.3 fit tables), but this document's own primary source (vLLM PR #56686, cited in §1.4) backs out ≈185,683 MiB (≈181.3 GiB) of addressable device memory from nvidia-smi's peak usage at 0.92 utilization, and the PR's own text independently labels the part '183 GB each' — a 3-8% disagreement with the pinned 180 GB that is stated but not resolved (this document deliberately keeps planning at 180 GB, per METHODOLOGY §8's convention of being conservative).

Prefill throughput — RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (gap X5-b200-prefill-roofline-13x-high): gpus/b200.md §9.3 held an est. row of 123,750 prefill tok/s/GPU for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (GEMM-only MFU formula) against this document's §3.1 measurement of 9,267 prefill tok/s/GPU from vLLM PR #56686's actual chunked-prefill step times — 13.4x lower, because the GEMM-only formula omits the indexer scan, top-k selection, Engram gathers and mHC mixing that dominate this model's prefill. gpus/b200.md §9.3 now prints the measured 9,267 tok/s/GPU (74,135 aggregate on 8 GPUs) with that cause annotated, so the two documents agree; no cost field in this entry changes, since every one of them was already built on the measured rate.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra (HGX 8-GPU, 268 GB/GPU as deployed, 2,144 GB/node)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 recommended (vLLM's B300 default is TP2 + mandatory --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'; 4 independent TP2 replicas per 8-GPU node is the max-throughput shape). Single node, 8-GPU NVLink-5 domain; no multi-node needed. KV latent is replicated per TP rank (confirmed against measured KV pools).
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native, but executed as W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations -> PTX .kind::mxf8f6f4 = 4,500 TFLOPS FP8 rate, NOT the 13,500 TFLOPS FP4 rate) + FP8 E4M3 32x32 UE8M0 for dense/attention/Engram + BF16 embed/head/vision; FP4 compressed KV (nvfp4_ds_mla) at 890 B/token
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 / FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (sm_103 satisfies the major==10 gate; FlashMLA PR #221 builds sm_100a and sm_103a); alternative FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 + FlashInfer top_k_varlen and HCA FP8 sparse-MLA decode (SM100 and SM103 since v0.6.18). No FlashAttention variant supports this gather-based sparse_attn operator on any GPU.
pairs.headline: Runs today on vLLM/SGLang nightlies; 2 GPUs minimum (TP2 + Engram host-offload), 4 recommended. The MXFP4 checkpoint executes W4A8 at the FP8 rate, so B300 matches B200 tok/s/GPU up to concurrency 64 and wins only on capacity (+245% at 128). $1.50-$3.04 per 1M output; the API at $0.60 is unbeatable on rented GPUs.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (B300 Blackwell Ultra, sm_103, 288 GB nominal / ~279 usable, 8.0 TB/s)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 on one GB300 compute tray (attention TP4 + MoE TP4 or EP4) — the only vLLM-"verified" GB300 shape and the one every published measurement uses. KV does NOT shard under TP (num_key_value_heads=1, MLA-shaped), so per-GPU KV = full KV per sequence; only DP-attention/DCP changes that. TP2 is possible with --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' onto Grace over the 900 GB/s NVLink-C2C link (untested on GB300, but B300 TP2 is the fastest measured config anywhere in the cross-GPU sweep). Rack = 18 independent TP4 replicas; EP72 is possible but 384 routed experts / 72 = 5.33 so it needs EPLB padding, and SGLang measured MoE TP4 beating EP4 at bs=1.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native, no dequant and no requant — routed experts (E2M1 + one E8M0 per 32) executed W4A8 against MXFP8 activations on the sm_103 block-scaled tcgen05 datapath; attention/shared/Engram FP8 E4M3 with UE8M0 scales on 32x32 tiles; embed/lm_head/vision BF16. KV cache runs in its native FP4 (E2M1 + one E4M3 per 16) via --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla = 890 B/token. The NVFP4 build (nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4, 527.27 GB) also runs natively and was validated on 4x GB300, but it is larger and has no published speedup.
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (gate capability.major==10, block 128, head size 512, nvfp4_ds_mla KV) — the fused norm-RoPE-attn-RoPE-cast mega kernel; alternatives FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 and FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41. Plus DeepseekV41IndexerBackend for the hierarchical sparse indexer and FlashInfer top_k_varlen / SGLang Lightning TopK for top-k. No FlashAttention release (FA2/FA3/FA4) implements this model's gather-based sparse_attn on any GPU. FlashMLA's own matrix says V4.1 sparse decode is "SM100 only" and lists no SM103 row — it runs on sm_103 anyway (measured), so support here is empirical, not documented.

pairs.headline: Runs natively today on 4 GB300 (TP4, vLLM/SGLang nightly): MXFP4 W4A8 + 890 B/token FP4 KV, 1,275 decode-only output tok/s/GPU at 25 ms TPOT (887 sustained end-to-end, measured), KV never binds. $3.92/1M output decode-only at OCI's $18/GPU-h ($5.64 sustained) — 6.5x DeepSeek's own API; only ownership economics close the gap.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA A100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 x DP2 (attention-DP) with EP8 on one HGX A100 8-GPU NVSwitch node; Engram tables host-offloaded (--engram-config cpu_offload); no multi-node (EP over 200 Gb/s IB is a trap)
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 experts -> Marlin W4A16 dequant-to-BF16; FP8 32x32 UE8M0 dense -> FP8-Marlin W8A16; memory win kept, compute win lost (sm_80 has no FP8/FP4 tensor cores)
pairs.attention_kernel: Community SM80 kernels: custom candidate-MQA (candidate_mqa_sm80.py) + patched sparse_attn_indexer, VLLM_SM80_CANDIDATE_MQA=1. No FlashMLA/DSA/FA3/FA4 on sm_80; FA2 exists but this model's gather-based sparse_attn is not a FlashAttention-shaped operator.

pairs.headline: Runs on 8x A100 via a community vLLM-backport fork + 24 SM80 patches (not upstream, not vendor-verified). MXFP4->Marlin W4A16, FP8 KV not FP4. Measured 3,040 tok/s @C128 (A800), TPOT 42 ms, $1.16-2.51/1M out. Never beats DeepSeek's off-peak API unless you already own the GPUs.

contradictions: Whether DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs on A100 at all: this document's verdict is 'yes, via a community vllm-backport fork + 24-file SM80 patch set, measured on 8x A800' — but research/gpus/a100.md §9 says 'No. MXFP4 has no sm_80 kernel... neither FlashMLA nor a sparse indexer kernel on sm_80', research/cross-cutting/inference-engines.md §3.2 says 'Treat A100 as out of scope and do not size a deployment on it', and research/cross-cutting/flash-attention.md §16.1 says 'A100 | none ... not deployable'. Already flagged prominently in the document's own headline note and §6 risk #2; not resolved by this audit.

KV cache bytes/token on A100: research/models/deepseek41f/architecture.md §5.2 and METHODOLOGY.md §8's deepseek41f model row state the FP4 KV cache (890 B/token) 'works identically on Hopper and Ampere — no FP4 tensor cores needed' (software-dequantised, no FP4 tensor core required). This a100.md document instead plans with 1,650 B/token (FP8, fp8_ds_mla) because that is what the one working SM80 community recipe actually configures, citing quantization-formats.md §8.1 and flash-attention.md §16.1 as scoping the 890 B/token path to sm_10x only. Already flagged in-document at §1.3 as a 'Stated disagreement, per METHODOLOGY §8'; not resolved by this audit — architecture.md/METHODOLOGY.md were left unchanged.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB GDDR7 (PCIe only, no NVLink; sm_120)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 + EP4, DCP1, single PCIe Gen5 chassis (no NVLink). Engram tables (202.76 GB / 188.83 GiB) must go to pinned host RAM or NVMe — 4 GPUs is infeasible with them HBM-resident. num_key_value_heads=1, so the CSA2 latent KV cannot be head-sharded: KV is replicated on every TP rank and DP-attention/DCP is unavailable (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 reports DCP unsupported). 8 GPUs fits with Engram in HBM but has no working measured stack; 16 needs two chassis and is ruled out for this card.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 experts executed natively as W4A8 via the FlashInfer/B12X SM12x fused-MoE path, FP8 32x32 UE8M0 dense/attention, BF16 embeddings/lm_head/ViT (510.29 GB checkpoint). KV runs FP8 at 1,650 B/token, NOT the shipped FP4 890 B/token cache. DISPUTED: METHODOLOGY 8 and gpus/rtx6000-pro.md 9g say MXFP4 falls back to Marlin W4A16 dequant on stock vLLM; quantization-formats.md 4.2/9.6 and both measured community builds say native b12x_fused_moe. Both true of different builds; no A/B published.
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (vLLM default on SM12x, FP8 KV dtype mandatory) / FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 / B12X_MLA_SPARSE in the measured community images, plus FlashInfer top_k_varlen for the DSA indexer. No FA2/FA3/FA4 (wrong operator shape; sm_120 also lacks tcgen05), no FlashMLA or FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (major 9/10 only), no TileLang DSA sparse-MLA (needs 202 KB SMEM, device allows 99 KB), no DeepGEMM (arch_major=12 unsupported).
pairs.headline: Runs today on 4 cards, but only on community B12X/SGLang builds: 740 tok/s at C8 (Server-Edition-scaled), FP8 KV not the shipped FP4, Engram offloaded to host. Stock vLLM on 8 GPUs collapses to 2.3-4.0 tok/s. Never beats DeepSeek's own $0.60/M API at any published rental price.

contradictions: None newly found. Two contradictions already exist between this document and foundation docs, but both are already explicitly flagged and resolved in-document per METHODOLOGY §8 (cited, not silently picked): (1) MXFP4 routed-expert execution path — METHODOLOGY §8 and gpus/rtx6000-pro.md §9g assume Marlin W4A16 dequant fallback on sm_120, while this document's §2 disagreement box concludes the measured builds run native b12x_fused_moe W4A8 (siding with quantization-formats.md §4.2/§9.6), citing that no A/B is published to settle it definitively. (2) Minimum GPU count — gpus/rtx6000-pro.md §9g computes 'at least 8 cards' assuming HBM-resident Engram tables; this document's §1.1 shows 4 cards suffice once the Engram tables are host/NVMe-offloaded (which vLLM's own recipe makes mandatory on H100/B300), and states this as a correction with both documents cited.

pairs.gpu: AMD Instinct MI355X 288GB (8-GPU UBB 2.0 platform, ROCm 7/10, gfx950)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 on half an 8-GPU node (2 independent TP4 replicas per baseboard); no EP flag, no DP-attention, no PD disagg on ROCm; TP2 infeasible with Engram resident (-1.94 GB KV budget) and only works with --engram-config cpu_offload; never TP16 (8-GPU scale-up domain, no NVL72 analogue). Routed experts + attention shard; the CSA2 latent KV and SWA ring are REPLICATED per TP rank (binding); Engram tables shard by row (~50.7 GB/GPU at TP4) ⚠️ unconfirmed on vLLM-ROCm.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native (E2M1 + E8M0/32 routed experts on CDNA4 scaled MFMA via AITER Composable Kernel a8w4, 10.1 PF dense) + FP8 E4M3 OCP 32x32 UE8M0 dense/attention/Engram (5.0 PF). Base checkpoint unconverted; the NVFP4 sibling build has no CDNA4 path (requant-to-MXFP4 only) and is larger with no published speedup. Exception: the checkpoint's FP4 main-KV layout has NO gfx950 kernel, so KV executes FP8 at 1,650 B/token, not the 890 B/token headline.
pairs.attention_kernel: ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE / ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4 + DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWABackend (AITER), SGLang DSA sub-backend `tilelang`. No FlashMLA, no FlashInfer, no FA3/FA4 on ROCm; FA2-CK exists but does not implement this model's gather-based sparse_attn. DSA/hierarchical-indexer kernel on gfx950 ⚠️ TO BE VERIFIED (no primary source). No published gfx950 sparse-MLA TFLOPS; best published gfx950 attention is 436-676 TFLOPS at hd256 from unmerged PRs, 3 of 4 measured on MI350X.
pairs.headline: Runs today on 4x MI355X (vLLM ROCm nightly, TP4) and is the one GPU where the checkpoint's MXFP4+FP8 is native end to end with Engram resident — but KV drops to FP8 (no FP4-KV kernel) and the decode stack runs at ~10.7% MBU, so $1.07-1.85/1M output est. vs $9.22 measured.

contradictions: METHODOLOGY.md §8 pins DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash KV at 890 B/token and states the FP4 cache 'is not Blackwell-only' (dequantised in software), while research/gpus/mi355x.md §2 states the opposite for this GPU: 'The pinned 890 B/token KV is the FP4-KV, Blackwell-kernel figure and has no gfx950 kernel.' This is already explicitly surfaced (not silently resolved) in research/models/deepseek41f/mi355x.md §1.1, which cites both documents and argues for the FP8/1,650 B/token reading on MI355X specifically (three engine-level citations: vLLM's nvfp4_ds_mla kernel gating, ROCm sparse-backend KV-dtype lists, and quantization-formats.md's NVFP4-KV-on-MI355X = ❌ marking). Flagging per audit instructions since it is a genuine disagreement between two foundation docs, even though this document does not pick one silently.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 in one HGX node, EP=1, plus --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'. 4 GPUs cannot hold 527.27 GB. Latent KV cannot be head-sharded (num_key_value_heads=1) so it is replicated per TP rank; embed, MoE routers, mHC and norms (1.675 GB) are also replicated. Without Engram offload TP8 leaves 0.62 GB/GPU of KV (5 seats at 128K); TP16 over InfiniBand is the alternative and costs METHODOLOGY's 20-40% multi-node comm penalty.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 dequant-to-BF16 (Marlin W4A16) — memory win kept, compute win lost; sm_90 has no FP4 tensor core. MTP/DSpark experts take a separate MXFP4 Marlin path in the same process (unvalidated). FP8/MXFP8 remainder (attention, shared experts, 188.8 GiB Engram) runs block-scaled FP8 with software FP32 promotion.
pairs.attention_kernel: vLLM FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (gate major in [9,10], block size 64 on SM90); SGLang --attention-backend dsa -> flashmla_sparse prefill / fa3 decode. FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (the nvfp4_ds_mla KV path) and FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 are SM100+ only. FlashMLA README says V4.1 sparse decode is SM100-only while vLLM admits major 9 — contested, ⚠️. FA2/FA3/FA4 matter only for the ViT.

pairs.headline: Fits 8xH100 but runs only as Marlin W4A16 — no FP4 math, vendor scopes it Blackwell-only, vLLM's NVFP4-MoE-on-Hopper bug is open. It is 16.99 GB larger and 2-5.7% more decode bytes than the MXFP4 base, which is the checkpoint to run. Needs TP8 + Engram CPU offload.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 on one HGX H200 node (8-GPU NVSwitch domain); EP8 + DP-attention possible but unpublished for this architecture. TP1/2/4 are infeasible (KV): 4 x 141 GB x 0.90 = 507.6 GB < 527.27 GB of weights. TP4 becomes feasible only with --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'. 16 GPUs buys 1.6x replicated-KV concurrency for a 20-40% comm tax and is not recommended.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 dequant-to-BF16 (Marlin W4A16). sm_90 has no FP4 tensor core, so the NVFP4 routed experts (58% of bytes) stay 4-bit in HBM but unpack to BF16 in registers and issue MMA at 989.5 dense TFLOPS. MTP/DSpark experts remain MXFP4 on a second Marlin path in the same process. KV is forced to FP8 fp8_ds_mla at 1,650 B/token; the architectural 890 B/token FP4 KV needs nvfp4_ds_mla -> FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 -> compute capability major==10 only.
pairs.attention_kernel: vLLM FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (gate capability.major in [9,10], block size 64 on SM90, KV dtypes auto/fp8_ds_mla/fp8). Sparse PREFILL on SM90 is measured at 640 TFLOPS (FlashMLA, H800 SXM5). Sparse DECODE for V4.1 is contested: FlashMLA's own matrix says "only available on SM100" while vLLM's gate accepts major 9 - unresolved. FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (the fused norm-RoPE-attn-RoPE-cast kernel, and the only nvfp4_ds_mla consumer) has no SM90 instantiation. FA2/FA3/FA4 are native but irrelevant to the language stack; they matter only for the ViT.
pairs.headline: Fits on 8xH200 (TP8, min = recommended) but is not supported today: NVIDIA declares Blackwell-only, sm_90 has no FP4 tensor core, so experts run Marlin W4A16 to BF16 and KV falls back to FP8 1,650 B/tok. Est. 4-5% slower and 4% less KV pool than the base MXFP4 build. Use the base checkpoint.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B200 (HGX 8-GPU, sm_100, 180 GB)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 minimum (only verified B200 shape, vLLM recipe meta.hardware.b200="verified"); recommended one HGX node as either TP8 (3.6x the KV budget, needed at >=32K ctx) or 2 x TP4 replicas (<=8K ctx). EP<=8 intra-node only; DP+EP (single_node_dep) is infeasible because 214.28 GB of non-expert weights, mostly the 202.76 GB Engram tables, replicate per DP rank vs 162 GB usable. TP1/TP2 infeasible (KV). TP16 crosses the 400 Gb/s scale-out fabric and hits the o_groups=8 divisibility limit.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native W4A4 (E2M1 gs16 + E4M3/16 + FP32 per-tensor) on the 384 routed experts of 40 backbone layers = 58% of bytes; MXFP4 native on the MTP/DSpark experts (ignore: mtp.*); FP8/MXFP8 E4M3 32x32 UE8M0 on attention, shared experts and the 188.8 GiB Engram tables (38.5% of bytes); BF16 on embed/lm_head/vision. Nothing is dequantised or requantised on sm_100.
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (nvfp4_ds_mla FP4 KV, best) / FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 / FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41, block size 128. SGLang: prefer --attention-backend trtllm_mla (1.2x prefill, 1.45x decode vs FlashMLA at kernel level on B200). FlashMLA sparse decode for V4.1 is SM100-only (700 TFLOPS, 1.71x H800); sparse prefill 1,450 TFLOPS. FA3 is rejected on Blackwell; FA4 applies only to the ViT. No linear-attention layers in this model.
pairs.headline: Runs natively on B200 (vLLM/SGLang, sm_100 NVFP4 W4A4); min TP4, recommended TP8. But on B200 this build is strictly worse than the 510.29 GB base: +5.5% decode bytes, -17% TP4 KV budget, no published speedup. S1 $0.57-1.32/1M out at conc 256; roofline ceiling $0.048-0.112.

contradictions: Fixed KV state per sequence: METHODOLOGY.md §8 pins 2.77 MiB = 2,906,112 B (43 layers incl. 3 MTP) for this model, while deepseek41fnvfp4/architecture.md §5.3/§5.6 computes 2,703,360 B = 2.58 MiB using only the 40 backbone layers. The audited doc uses METHODOLOGY's 2,906,112 B and states why; this is a pre-existing, already-disclosed disagreement between METHODOLOGY.md and architecture.md, not something this document introduced or silently resolved.

B200 HBM per GPU: METHODOLOGY.md §8 and gpus/b200.md §2 both pin 180 GB (as-deployed, used throughout the audited doc), while vLLM PR #56686 reports '183 GB each' measured on a real 8×B200 node (a 1.7% gap = ~11% of the TP4 KV budget). gpus/b200.md §2 itself leaves the underlying GB-vs-GiB question open (⚠️ TO BE VERIFIED against nvidia-smi); the audited doc inherits rather than resolves this open question.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra (HGX 8-GPU, 268 GB per GPU as deployed, 2,144 GB per node)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 (EP4 optional), single HGX B300 node, NVLink 5 — no multi-node fabric needed. TP2 only if the 188.83 GiB Engram tables leave HBM (vLLM --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' or kern's row-sharded -hbm manifest); TP2 with the full checkpoint resident is infeasible (KV): 2x268 GB vs 527.27 GB of weights = -27.8 GB/GPU budget. The single latent KV stream (num_key_value_heads=1) cannot be head-sharded, so KV is replicated per rank under plain TP unless DP-attention/DCP is enabled.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native W4A4 on sm_103 tcgen05 (.kind::mxf4nvf4) for the 58.0% of bytes that are backbone routed experts; the rest executes at its source precision — Engram tables MXFP8/FP8 (38.5% of bytes, gather not GEMM), attention + shared experts FP8 E4M3 32x32 UE8M0, MTP/DSpark experts MXFP4, embeddings/LM head BF16, mHC FP32. No dequant or requant path needed on Blackwell.
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (the only backend that unlocks nvfp4_ds_mla = FP8 SWA cache + NVFP4 compressed cache, gated major==10, satisfied by sm_103); alternatives FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 / FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41, block 128; SGLang --attention-backend dsa. FlashInfer NVFP4 paged-KV sparse decode/prefill for SM103 merged 2026-09-18 (PR #4982). FA2/FA3 irrelevant; FA4 only for the ViT. Risk: FlashMLA's matrix documents V4.1 sparse decode as SM100-only and sglang#27384 reports a device-side assert in flash_mla_sparse_fwd on B300/sm_103 that is token-exact on B200.
pairs.headline: Fits and runs natively: 4xB300 TP4 (2 with Engram off-GPU), NVFP4 W4A4 on sm_103. But nobody has measured this checkpoint on B300, and at saturated batch its experts are 5.7% more bytes/step than the MXFP4 base on a bandwidth-bound decode: expect ~5% slower, not faster.

contradictions: No contradictions found between this document and the foundation docs (METHODOLOGY.md, architecture.md §3-6, gpus/b300.md §2/3/8/9) beyond what the document already states itself in §1.1's 'Disagreements' box. Prices match cloud-pricing.md §5.7 exactly. One internal (not foundation-doc) inconsistency was flagged in the new Audit log rather than silently resolved: §3.2's decode-step formula divides the shared latent KV-cache read by n_gpus=4 (the 'optimistic' KV-sharded-across-ranks reading), but §5.3's actually-validated launch commands run plain --tp 4 with no DP-attention/DCP, which per §1.3's own analysis means KV should be replicated per rank instead (the 'conservative' reading, which §1.4's own table shows gives 4x lower max-concurrency: 869 vs 3,479 at 128K). This is the same ambiguity §6.3 open-question #11 already names, but that item doesn't note that §3.2's own arithmetic silently picks one side of it while its header says plain 'TP4'. Recomputing §3.2-§4.4 under the conservative assumption would materially change every TPOT/TTFT/cost number there — a substantive re-derivation, not an in-place fix — so it was left flagged rather than resolved either way, per the audit instructions not to silently pick a side.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (per-GPU B300 "Blackwell Ultra", sm_103, 288 GB nameplate / ~279 GB as deployed, 8.0 TB/s, 15,000 TFLOPS dense NVFP4)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 on one NVL72 compute tray (the only shape NVIDIA validated, both vLLM and SGLang). TP8 or TP4+DP2 across two trays when KV headroom or lower single-stream latency matters; o_groups=8 bounds clean output-projection sharding at TP<=8. Full rack = 18 independent TP4 replicas (or 9x TP8) behind a router, NOT one 72-way EP domain: the model's 527 GB fits in 4 GPUs, so wide-EP is a throughput optimisation rather than a feasibility requirement, DeepEP publishes no SM103 row, and the only published EP run on this model family (B200 SGLang TP4/EP4) is 8x slower than vLLM EP1. Under pure TP the MLA latent KV (num_key_value_heads=1) is replicated on every rank; DP-attention or DCP is required to make aggregate KV scale with GPU count. 1P1D disaggregation (TP4 prefill + TP4 decode) suits the CED split (7.89 B active prefill vs 15.75 B decode) and is run as a per-commit GB300 Slurm CI job by TokenSpeed — but for the base MXFP4 repo, not this one.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native (W4A4, group 16) on the routed experts = 58.0% of bytes, executed on sm_103 tcgen05 block-scaled tensor cores via flashinfer_trtllm_routed / VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=1 at 15,000 TFLOPS dense. The other 42% executes at its source precision, also natively: FP8/MXFP8 Engram tables (38.5% of bytes), FP8 attention and shared experts, BF16 embed/LM head/ViT, FP32 mHC, plus MXFP4 MTP/DSpark experts (kept, not converted). No dequant, no requant, no Marlin fallback anywhere. KV cache is architectural FP4 (E2M1 + one E4M3 per 16), 890 B/token, reachable only via nvfp4_ds_mla on major==10.
pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (vLLM; major==10 only; the only backend accepting nvfp4_ds_mla = "V4.1 fp8 SWA cache + NVFP4 compressed cache", i.e. the kernel that realises the 890 B/token figure). Alternatives on sm_103: FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (block 128) and FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (FlashInfer NVFP4 paged-KV sparse PR #4982 merged 2026-09-18, SM100/SM103). CSA2 indexer top-k via FlashInfer top_k_varlen Blackwell radix kernel / SGLang Lightning TopK. SGLang path: --attention-backend dsa, trtllm sub-backend default on Blackwell. FA2/FA3 irrelevant (FA3 does not run on Blackwell at all); FA4 matters only for the ViT and has a known sm_103 arch-check crash in some builds. No CK/AITER (AMD-only).
pairs.headline: Runs natively on GB300 (NVIDIA's only tested HW; vLLM/SGLang main-branch, TP4, 4 GPUs, NVFP4 W4A4 experts). Decode is memory-bound, so NVFP4's extra scale byte makes it est. 2-5% slower and 4.25 GB/GPU larger than the MXFP4 base. S1 est. $1.24/1M out at OCI $18/GPU-h; no published perf exists.

Already declared inline in this doc's §1.1; effect is ≤2% on concurrency.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA A100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU; sm_80, no FP8/FP4 tensor cores)
pairs.parallelism: TP8+EP8 on one HGX A100 baseboard (measured proxy uses TP4xDP2+EP8+EPLB); Engram tables CPU-offloaded to fit; EP is mandatory not optional; no multi-node — 16 GPUs = 2 replicas, never TP16 (25 GB/s IB vs 600 GB/s NVLink)
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 dequant-to-BF16 via Marlin W4A16 (no FP4/FP8 MMA on sm_80; MARLIN routes to nvfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config so the W4A4 group-16 activation scales are discarded) — and not runnable today for lack of any sm_80 attention backend
pairs.attention_kernel: None upstream: FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 requires CC 9/10, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 CC 10/12, FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 CC 10 (so nvfp4_ds_mla 890 B/token KV is unreachable; FP8 1,650 B/token instead). Community fork substitutes Triton BF16 sparse-MLA + sparse-SWA + fp8_mqa_logits_triton indexer. FA2 runs, but only for the ViT.
pairs.headline: Not runnable: no engine admits DeepseekV41ForCausalLM on sm_80; NVIDIA scopes this build to Blackwell. Hardware fits at 8 GPUs with Engram CPU-offload. Figures are the measured base-MXFP4 proxy on 8xA800; the NVFP4 build is ~6% slower, 17 GB larger, zero gain on A100.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB GDDR7 (PCIe only, no NVLink; sm_120)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 (+EP8) single chassis, PCIe Gen5, no NVLink; KV cache replicated on every rank (num_key_value_heads=1, DCP unsupported); Engram tables (202.76 GB) in pinned host RAM or NVMe, not HBM. TP4 is the arithmetic minimum but leaves only 1.27 GB KV/GPU at util 0.90.

pairs.attention_kernel: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 (SM12x branch, FP8 KV dtype mandatory) / FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 / B12X_MLA_SPARSE; FlashInfer top_k_varlen for the DSA indexer. No FlashMLA (major in [9,10]), no FA3/FA4 (no tcgen05), no trtllm-gen FMHA (no SM120/121 cubins, none planned), no TileLang DSA (needs 202 KB shared memory vs the device's 99 KB).
pairs.headline: Fits (4 GPU min with Engram in host RAM, 8 recommended) but no engine has served this exact checkpoint on sm_120. NVFP4 is strictly worse than the MXFP4 base here: +16.99 GB eats 77% of the 4-GPU KV budget and it gives up the base native W4A8 expert path for Marlin W4A16 dequant.

pairs.gpu: AMD Instinct MI355X 288GB (gfx950, CDNA4, 8-GPU UBB 2.0 platform, ROCm 7/10)
pairs.parallelism: TP4 on half a UBB baseboard, EP off, no PD/wide-EP (scale-up domain is 8); KV latent + SWA ring replicated on every TP rank; Engram tables row-sharded (⚠️ unconfirmed on vLLM-ROCm). TP2 infeasible (weights, -10.75 GB), TP8 spare headroom, never TP16.
pairs.weight_format_used: BF16 dequant emulation — vLLM Nvfp4QuantizationEmulationTritonExperts unpacks NVFP4 every forward step (CDNA4 has no NVFP4 matrix path; Marlin W4A16 fallback is CUDA-only; SGLang quark_mxfp4 requant unavailable for DeepseekV41 on gfx950). Attention/Engram stay FP8/MXFP8 native; MTP/DSpark experts stay MXFP4 native; KV forced to FP8 1,650 B/token.
pairs.attention_kernel: ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE / ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4 + DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWABackend (AITER); FP8 KV only — nvfp4_ds_mla needs FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 at compute capability major==10. No FA3/FA4/FlashMLA/FlashInfer on ROCm; DSA indexer kernel on gfx950 ⚠️ unconfirmed.
pairs.headline: Fits at TP4 (121 GB KV budget) but no engine serves it today: SGLang's NVFP4-to-MXFP4 requant has no DSV4.1 gfx950 support (PR #39186 closed) and vLLM-ROCm falls back to BF16 dequant emulation. 17 GB bigger and 7.5% slower than the base MXFP4 build. Use the base.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP2, replicated (4 x TP2 replicas per HGX H100 node). TP is limited to {1,2,4,8} by shape: 24 query heads exclude TP16, 16 GDN key heads exclude TP3/6/12, and only 4 KV heads mean TP8 replicates the KV cache (each rank holds 1/4, not 1/8). A replica never leaves one NVLink domain, so no multi-node fabric is ever needed. Use TP4 if 128K traffic dominates; avoid TP8 (MBU falls to 0.35). TP1 works and is the minimum.
pairs.weight_format_used: FP8 E4M3 block-128 native (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) on sm_90 Transformer Engine tensor cores. BF16 also native but leaves only 12.44 GB of KV budget. NVFP4/MXFP4 have no tensor core on Hopper: NVFP4 loads only as Marlin W4A16 dequant (memory win, no FLOPS win) and SGLang greys out every NVFP4 cell on SM90; MXFP4 does not load on NVIDIA. INT4 W4A16 (RedHatAI) is the alternative 4-bit path but its prefill runs at the BF16 rate.
pairs.attention_kernel: Two kernel families. 16 gated-GQA layers (head_dim 256, 24:4): FA3 is the vLLM/SGLang default on SM90 (740 TFLOPS FP16 ~75% of peak, ~1.2 PFLOPS FP8; FP8 KV runs attention itself in the quantised domain). FA4 builds for SM90 but is not the default and its FP8 path is SM100-only; FlashInfer is what SGLang's Hopper recipe pins. 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers: vLLM selects FlashInfer GDN prefill ("Hopper (SM90) - no further constraints", JIT warm-up) plus the fused CUDA GDN decode kernel; SGLang stays on Triton because its FlashInfer-GDN auto-select gates on SM100/SM103. No MLA and no sparse/DSA indexer apply to this model.
pairs.headline: Runs on H100 (vLLM h100 profile + FP8/INT4 variants) but nobody has published a single number for this pair. FP8 is mandatory: BF16 leaves 12.4 GB of KV budget. 2xH100 TP2 is the shape: 4,027 tok/s/GPU at 15.9 ms TPOT, $0.22-0.48/1M out. Capacity, not latency, is the ceiling.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP1 x 8 replicas per HGX node (both vendor-verified profiles are TP1). TP4 x 2 gives +35% node tok/s and ~2x node concurrency at the same 50ms SLO but is unverified for this pair. TP>4 stops shrinking per-GPU KV (num_key_value_heads=4). No EP (dense model), no PP, never multi-node.
pairs.weight_format_used: FP8 E4M3 block-128 native (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, 30.870 GB) — BF16 also native; NVFP4/INT4 load only as Marlin/Machete W4A16 dequant and are 11% slower than FP8 at the throughput point; MXFP4 does not load on NVIDIA

pairs.headline: Vendor-verified on 1xH200 (SGLang 0.5.19+, vLLM 0.17.0+) at FP8; NVFP4 only dequants to Marlin W4A16 and lands 11% below FP8. Capacity, not TPOT, binds: 168 concurrent 4.6K seqs at 24ms. $0.16-0.45/1M out. No tok/s or TTFT measurement exists for this pair.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B200 (HGX 8-GPU, sm_100, 180 GB)
pairs.parallelism: TP1 per replica, 8 data-parallel replicas per HGX node (vLLM compatible_strategies = single_node_tp). TP4 only to buy KV headroom; TP8 duplicates the 4 KV heads (1.45x concurrency at 8K, 1.07x at 128K); TP16 crosses the 400 Gb/s scale-out fabric for nothing.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native (9,000 TFLOPS dense) with FP8 attention/GDN projections — Inferact/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 26.381 GB is vLLM's b200-listed variant (the 21.92 GB nvidia/ export lists only rtx_pro_6000 + dgx_spark_gb10). FP8 block-128 is the conservative native alternative; MXFP4 does not load on NVIDIA; INT4 runs Marlin W4A16 on the BF16 math line.
pairs.attention_kernel: trtllm_mha for the 16 full-attention layers (GQA 24:4, head_dim 256) — SGLang forbids FlashInfer for hybrid-GDN full attention on SM100, FA3 is unsupported on Blackwell, and FA4 hd256 is reported failing at graph capture for the same qwen3_5 family (sglang#39515) while vLLM silently drops to FA2 unless block size is a multiple of 128. GDN layers: FlashInfer GDN prefill fast path (head_k_dim 128 + CUDA>=13 + bf16 state + chunked-prefill 1-8192), CuteDSL GDN prefill opt-in SM100-only, fused CUDA GDN decode kernel.
pairs.headline: Fits and runs on one B200 at TP1 in every precision (NVFP4 native, 131.6 GB KV budget, 199 concurrent 8K sessions at FP8 KV / S=5), but nobody has published a single tok/s for this pair: est. $0.185-0.433 per 1M output interactive, $0.150-0.351 at max throughput.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra (HGX 8-GPU, 268 GB/GPU as deployed, 2,144 GB/node)
pairs.parallelism: TP1, 8 independent replicas per node (data-parallel replication). TP only buys KV budget and stops buying it past TP4 because the model has 4 KV heads (TP8 replicates them ×2). Never multi-node.
pairs.weight_format_used: Mixed NVFP4 + FP8 + BF16, all native on sm_103: NVFP4 W4A4 on the 64 MLPs + lm_head (71.7% of GEMM FLOPs), FP8 E4M3 on the 16 self-attn + 48 GDN projections (28.2%), BF16 vision tower / norms / MTP head. 21.92 GB (nvidia, RadixArk) or 26.38 GB (Inferact, the build vLLM's b300 profile points at).
pairs.attention_kernel: Full attention (16 layers, head_dim 256): FA4 hd256 2-CTA native on sm_103 but mutually exclusive with quantized KV in vLLM (silent FA2 fallback); FlashInfer illegal for hybrid-GDN on SM100/103; trtllm_mha had an SM103 high-concurrency hang (sglang#21904); Triton is the safe lane. GDN (48 layers): FlashInfer GDN prefill fast path auto-selects on SM100/SM103 with CUDA>=13 and BF16 recurrent state; CuteDSL GDN prefill opt-in (B200/B300 only); fused CUDA / FlashInfer GDN decode. No sparse/DSA indexer in this model.
pairs.headline: Fits 1 B300 in every precision; run TP1 x8 replicas, not TP8. S1 $0.165-0.334/1M out, blended $0.060-0.122; break-even vs Qwen's API at 7% utilisation. But B300's 1.5x FP4 reaches only 71.7% of GEMM FLOPs (28% is FP8 = B200 rate), and no one has measured this pair.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (per B300, 288 GB nominal / ~279 GB usable, sm_103)
pairs.parallelism: TP1, one GPU per replica (vLLM `single_node_tp`, `"gb300": "verified"`; SGLang v0.5.19 all 5 checkpoints verified). KV shards only to TP4 (4 KV heads) and GDN state only to TP16 (16 key heads), so TP>4 buys latency, not capacity; TP4 is the shape NVIDIA and RadixArk publish for a tray. 18/36/72 GPUs are replica counts, not TP groups. Wide-EP is not applicable — the model is dense, there are no experts. No multi-node fabric ever needed.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native (W4A4, tcgen05 block-scaled) on the 64 MLPs + lm_head = 71.7% of GEMM params, plus FP8 native (block-128) on the 16 attention and 48 GDN projections; BF16 vision tower (0.921 GB, DP-replicated), MTP head (0.849 GB) and norms. 21.92 GB total. FP8 E4M3 KV cache. Blended effective dense prefill peak 9,584 TFLOPS, not 15,000.
pairs.attention_kernel: 16 full-attention (GQA 24:4, head_dim 256) layers: FA4 hd256 2-CTA Blackwell kernel (sm_103a path merged in fa4-v4.0.0.beta22) — only if block size is a multiple of 128, else vLLM silently falls back to FA2; SGLang on SM100/SM103 permits only triton / trtllm_mha / fa4 for hybrid-GDN full attention, never FlashInfer (hence the GB300 cells omit --attention-backend). 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers: FlashInfer GDN prefill fast path (auto-selected on SM100/SM103 with CUDA>=13, head_k_dim 128, BF16 recurrent state, chunked-prefill 1-8192) + fused CUDA GDN decode kernel; CuteDSL GDN prefill opt-in on SM10.x. No sparse/DSA indexer in this model.
pairs.headline: Runs today on 1 GPU (vLLM + SGLang GB300-verified; NVFP4 W4A4 + FP8 attn + FP8 KV). Est. 14,411 tok/s/GPU at bs=414, TPOT 28.7 ms — S1 and S4 coincide because the KV/state pool binds before the 50 ms SLO. $0.347/1M out at OCI's $18.00/GPU-h, the only published rate. Dense: wide-EP N/A.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA A100 SXM4 80GB (HGX 8-GPU, sm_80)
pairs.parallelism: TP1 per replica x DP8 per HGX node (model fits one GPU in every precision). TP2/TP4 only to cut TTFT or buy long-context KV budget; TP8 duplicates the 4 KV heads (2x KV bytes/token/GPU); never multi-node — A100 has no NVLink domain beyond one baseboard and 200 Gb/s IB is 24x slower.
pairs.weight_format_used: INT4 W4A16 native-path/dequant math (Marlin, RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4, 19.45 GB) + FP8 KV (storage-only, no FA3) + bf16 GDN state. BF16 55.56 GB is the only natively-executed format but leaves 12.44 GB budget. FP8 checkpoint = W8A16 Marlin in theory, but vllm#55008 (open) selects CUTLASS FP8 on SM80 and asserts. NVFP4/MXFP4 not runnable.
pairs.attention_kernel: FlashAttention-2 on the 16 GQA head_dim-256 layers (vLLM selector: sm90->FA3, sm100->FA4, else FA2; FA2 measured 230 TFLOPS = 73% of peak on A100). Gated-DeltaNet on the other 48 layers: Triton/FLA prefill (FlashInfer GDN fast path is SM90/SM10x/SM12x only) + vLLM's fused CUDA GDN decode kernel, explicitly gated at has_device_capability(80). No FA3, FA4, FlashMLA, DSA indexer, or FP8-domain attention math.
pairs.headline: Runnable on paper, verified by nobody — no engine publishes an A100 profile (vLLM hw/a100.json is 404). One GPU fits every precision; INT4-Marlin + FP8 KV holds 92 concurrent 4K seqs at 45 ms TPOT. Decode saturates at ~2,030 tok/s/GPU because no format accelerates math on sm_80. $0.22–0.47/1M out.

contradictions: RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (gap C1-a100-capacity-basis): 80 GB decimal is the single A100 planning basis tree-wide, usable_hbm 72.0 GB = 67.06 GiB/GPU; the nvidia-smi 81,920 MiB = 80 GiB = 85.90 GB reading is an unsourced binary derivation kept only as a labelled TO BE VERIFIED +7.4% sensitivity (METHODOLOGY §8, gpus/a100.md §2). gpus/a100.md §9 was recomputed onto the decimal budget (its Qwen3.8-27B FP8+FP8KV 1-GPU cell 99 -> 87 at S=1). qwen3827b/a100.md already planned on 80 GB decimal, so no number in this pair moved; its §1.0 disagreement box became a one-line pointer and §6 risk 5 is marked resolved.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB GDDR7 (PCIe only, no NVLink; sm_120)
pairs.parallelism: TP1 — one GPU per replica, scale by data-parallel replication. TP>1 is discouraged: TP4 over PCIe Gen5 measured 6–7 tok/s vs 46–49 with TP2+PP2 (~85% overhead), and num_key_value_heads=4 caps clean KV sharding at TP4 (KV replicates past that). No NVLink, no multi-node.
pairs.weight_format_used: NVFP4 native W4A4 dense GEMM (nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 21.92 GB: NVFP4 MLPs + lm_head, FP8 attn/GDN projections, BF16 ViT+MTP+norms) with FP8 E4M3 KV and bf16 GDN state. Dense-only quantisation, so it misses the broken sm_120 MoE grouped-GEMM path entirely.
pairs.attention_kernel: FlashInfer FA2 backend (--attention-backend flashinfer) for the 16 GQA head_dim-256 layers; Triton/FlashInfer GDN kernels for the 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers. No FA3 (9.x only), no FA4 in vLLM (9.x/10.x/11.x), no FlashMLA/trtllm-gen cubins on SM12x. Attention runs BF16 whatever the weight format — no FP8 e4m3 prefill kernel on SM120/121.
pairs.headline: Fits one card at every precision; NVFP4 W4A4 runs natively on sm_120 because the model is dense. TP1 + replication only. S1 bs=64 TPOT 31 ms, 2,052 tok/s/GPU, $0.24-0.56/1M out; S4 bs=111, $0.19-0.44. Break-even vs Qwen Cloud at 9% utilisation.

pairs.gpu: AMD Instinct MI355X 288GB (CDNA 4, gfx950, 8-GPU UBB 2.0 node)
pairs.parallelism: TP1, scaled by data-parallel replicas (8 per node). TP4 only if one endpoint must hold more KV than one GPU; TP8 is net-negative because the 4 GQA KV heads cannot shard past TP4 and get duplicated (2169 vs 2848 concurrent 8K seqs per node). No EP (dense), no PD (Dynamo has no ROCm support), no multi-node need.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native (amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4, W4A4 g32 E8M0, 19.798 GB measured from the safetensors header; lm_head/MTP/vision stay BF16) on the 10.1 PF dense path. FP8 block-128 (30.870 GB, 5.0 PF) is the conservative fallback. NVFP4 not native (requant to MXFP4 or BF16 dequant); INT4 W4A16 is a Triton dequant path with no published MFMA rate.
pairs.attention_kernel: CK FlashAttention-2 for the 16 GQA head_dim-256 layers (AITER's tuned ASM hd256 kernel is MHA-only and still an open PR, so 24:4 GQA falls back to CK ~436 TFLOPS class); AITER Triton kernels for the 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers (FlashInfer GDN prefill and the fused CUDA GDN decode kernel are CUDA-gated). vLLM backend ROCM_AITER_FA with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1. No FA3/FA4/FlashInfer/FlashMLA on gfx950. FP8 KV native; FP4 KV unsupported.
pairs.headline: Runnable today on vLLM-ROCm, 1 GPU TP1. AMD does ship an MXFP4 build (amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4, 19.798 GB), closing architecture.md gap 14. 288 GB makes this pair capacity-bound, not latency-bound: $0.211/1M out interactive, $0.195 max-throughput, at OCI's sole $8.60/GPU-hr.

contradictions: mi355x.md's TTFT-90%-hit column (all three §3.3 tables), the §4.4 'Effect of prefix caching' table, and the '$0.080 → $0.056' blended-cost claim in §4.4's prose compute a prefix-cache hit as literally free (cost multiplier 1-h). METHODOLOGY.md §6 explicitly says to assume a cache hit costs 10% of the uncached prefill cost (multiplier 1-0.9h) unless measured. Under the correct METHODOLOGY rule: 90%-hit effective prefill tok/s should be ~188,400 (doc says 357,963), $/1M input at 90% hit should be ~$0.0126 (doc says $0.0067), and the 90%-hit blended cost should be ~$0.062 (doc says $0.056). The 'free' convention is applied consistently across every affected cell (not a one-off slip) and is undisclosed -- §4.2's blended baseline elsewhere correctly applies and cites the 10% rule 'verbatim'. RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (gap C8): the doc now costs hits at 1-0.9h -- §4.4 reads 65,084 / 188,400 eff. prefill tok/s and $0.0367 / $0.0127 per 1M input at 50%/90% hit, blended $0.080 -> $0.062; the §3.3 TTFT columns keep 1-h (latency only) and say so in the column header.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP32 + EP32 across 4 HGX nodes (IB/RoCE). TP is hard-capped at 32 by gcd(96 heads, 7168 hidden); >32 GPUs = replicas or DP-attention, never wider TP. No DCP and no wide-EP/MegaMoE on SM90.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 dequant-to-BF16 in-kernel (Marlin W4A16, `--moe-runner-backend marlin` / `--moe-backend marlin`); non-expert tensors stay BF16. H100 has no FP4/MX tensor cores, so 4-bit buys capacity only. Measured resident footprint is 1.31x the checkpoint share (59.63 GiB/GPU at TP32 vs 48.78 GB theory).
pairs.attention_kernel: FlashMLA (SM90) for the 24 Gated-MLA decode layers + FA3 prefill (measured: decode_backend=flashmla, prefill_backend=fa3); native fused CUDA KDA decode for the 69 linear layers (FlashInfer's faster fused_kda_decode is Blackwell-gated); AttnRes runs JIT (SGLANG_K3_ATTN_RES_MODE=jit). No sparse/DSA indexer in this model. TOKENSPEED_MLA/TRTLLM_MLA/CUTEDSL_MLA unavailable on SM90.
pairs.headline: Runnable only at 32x H100 (4 HGX nodes, TP32/EP32) on the Marlin W4A16 dequant path - no FP4 silicon. The TPOT<=50ms interactive SLO is unreachable (best 113ms est., 172ms measured). Max-throughput output costs $32-70/1M vs Moonshot's $15 list: self-hosting loses at every price tier.

contradictions: research/gpus/h100.md §2 states Kimi-K3 needs ≥24 H100 (3 nodes) to fit, using the naive checkpoint_bytes/n_gpus share (65.0 GB/GPU at N=24). research/models/kimik3/h100.md §1.2-1.3 (backed by the measured Marlin resident-weight multiplier from two independent SGLang runs) shows N=24 is actually 79.5 GB/GPU against an 80 GB card — it does not fit, and 24 is not even a valid TP size (7168/24 is not integral) — the true minimum is 32 GPUs. This was already flagged inline in kimik3/h100.md §1.3 as a correction to gpus/h100.md, but gpus/h100.md itself has not been updated, so the two foundation docs still disagree on Kimi-K3's minimum H100 count (24 vs 32). Left unresolved per instructions rather than silently edited. RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (gap C6-kimi-k3-minimum-gpu-counts): gpus/h100.md §2 now states ≥ 32 H100 (4 HGX nodes, TP32/EP32) in both its Kimi-K3 row and the bullet below it, with the KV budget and seat counts recomputed at N=32 in python3 (615.10 GB = 572.86 GiB → 260/151 on the naive share; 127.04 GB = 118.32 GiB → 53/31 on the measured 64.03 GB/GPU resident), and kimik3/h100.md §1.3's per-rank 21 @ 8K / 2 @ 128K remains the planning pair. min_gpus here was already 32 and did not change; the matching A100 holdout (kimik3/a100.min_gpus 24 → 32) was fixed in the same pass.

RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (final consistency pass): interactive.cost_per_1m_output_usd_low/high were 3217.55/6917.74, a 0.015% stale artefact of an unrounded 113.115 ms TPOT that kimik3/h100.md's own audit log (gap X3) already superseded with 113.1 ms -> $3,217.07/$6,916.69 in its §4.1 table, while claiming (inaccurately) that pairs.json already matched. Recut to 3217.07/6916.69; research/README.md §6 footnote 1 recut in the same pass.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141GB (HGX 8-GPU)
pairs.parallelism: TP16 + EP16 across 2x HGX 8-GPU nodes over 400G IB/EFA (vLLM multi_node_tp, SGLang low-latency/balanced cells); TP32+EP32 on 4 nodes for the high-throughput profile. TP hard-capped at 32 by gcd(96 heads, 7168 hidden). No DCP on H200 (not in any recipe), multi_node_dep explicitly unsupported. MLA KV replicated per TP rank; KDA state shards only by attention-TP width.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 dequant-to-BF16 in-kernel via Marlin W4A16 (sm_90 has no FP4/MX tensor core); measured +5.3% weight bytes from the Marlin repack (102.75 GB/GPU at TP16 vs 97.56 theoretical). Faster alternative: requantised INT4-g128 + FP8-activation (vessl/Kimi-K3-W4AFP8), measured +17.9% throughput on the same 16xH200.
pairs.attention_kernel: FlashMLA SM90 MQA for the 24 Gated-MLA decode layers (--decode-attention-backend flashmla / --attention-backend FLASHMLA); vLLM native fused CUDA fused_kda_decode for the 69 KDA layers (is_device_capability(90)); fla chunk_kda (Triton) for KDA prefill; MoonViT-V2 on FA2. FlashInfer fused KDA decode is Blackwell-only. No sparse/DSA indexer exists in this model. MLA prefill kernel on sm_90 is unverified.

pairs.headline: Runnable on 16xH200 (2 nodes, TP16+EP16); MXFP4 runs via Marlin W4A16 dequant - no FP4 on sm_90. Measured 21.5 decode-only out tok/s/GPU at 23 ms TPOT with DSpark (17.4 sustained end-to-end); decode is latency-bound (2-20% MBU). $51-$102/1M output decode-only ($64-$127 sustained) vs Moonshot's $15 API. Break-even $2.44-$3.51/GPU-h beats no published H200 price.

contradictions: research/models/kimik3/h200.md §1.3 gives 16×H200 max concurrency at 8K/32K/128K as 34–50/12–25/3–6 (per-GPU MLA-KV-replicated, KDA-state-divided-by-attnTP accounting), which numerically contradicts research/gpus/h200.md §2's own summary table for the same pair (169/148/98, aggregate-budget accounting). Remaining ⚠️: confirm against a booted engine's reported KV pool (benchmark B2).

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B200 (HGX 8-GPU, sm_100, 180 GB as deployed)
pairs.parallelism: 16 GPUs = 2 HGX B200 nodes. Recommended: PP2 x TP8 + DCP8 + EP8 (SGLang Balanced) — PP splits the 93 layers across the two nodes so every per-layer collective stays inside one 1.8 TB/s NVLink island, and DCP8 is the only axis that shards the otherwise TP-replicated MLA KV (225 vs 54 concurrent at 128K). vLLM ships flat TP16 (multi_node_tp, "verified") and offers no DCP outside single_node_tp; DSPARK forces pp_size==1 so it collapses PP2xTP8 -> TP16 / PP2xDCPEP8 -> DCPEP16. 8 GPUs cannot hold the weights at all (196.3 GB/GPU vs 180 GB physical). Keep EP <= 8: the scale-out fabric is 0.8 TB/s/node, half B300's.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native, executed W4A8 on the FlashInfer trtllm-gen SiTU MoE runner (no dequant, no requant). Only 46.7% of active params are MXFP4, so Amdahl caps the FP4 speedup at 1.87x. FP8 E4M3 KV is mandatory (TOKENSPEED_MLA force-rewrites --kv-cache-dtype to fp8).
pairs.attention_kernel: 24 Gated-MLA layers: TOKENSPEED_MLA (vLLM B200 recipe; 10.x-only, FP8 KV required) / trtllm_mla, with cutedsl_mla taking decode under DCP. 69 KDA layers: FlashInfer fused_kda_decode, gate is compute_capability in ((10,0),(10,3)) — B200 and B300 only — measured 1.33x the vLLM native fused kernel at one row, geomean 1.13x; chunk_kda from flash-linear-attention for prefill. MoonViT-V2 tower asks for FA2. FA3 is refused on Blackwell; no sparse/DSA indexer exists for this model.
pairs.headline: Runnable, but never on one node: 16x B200 (2 HGX nodes) minimum, PP2xTP8+DCP8+EP8, native MXFP4 W4A8. Interactive $16.34-$38.78/1M out NOSPEC, $2.63-$6.24 with DSPARK; max-throughput $3.81-$9.05. Roofline calibrated to 7 measured InferenceX B200 rows.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra (HGX 8-GPU, 268 GB/GPU as deployed, 2,144 GB/node)
pairs.parallelism: TP8 + DCP8 on one HGX node (vLLM --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8; SGLang --tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8). EP8 optional but conflicts with DCP's a2a buffers. PP/DP-attention/wide-EP only make sense at 16-32 GPUs. KDA state pool shards only by attention-TP; MLA KV is TP-replicated and shards only under DCP.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native (W4A8) — the shipped QAT checkpoint runs unchanged on the sm_103 FP4 datapath via FlashInfer trtllm-gen SiTU kernels; no dequant, no requant. NVFP4 builds exist and are measurably slower (TPOT 10.12 vs 8.51 ms at c=1) and larger (+49 GB).
pairs.attention_kernel: TOKENSPEED_MLA (10.x-only, FP8-KV-required) for the 24 Gated-MLA layers, prefill and decode; FlashInfer fused_kda_decode for the 69 KDA linear-attention layers (gate is compute_capability in ((10,0),(10,3)) — B200/B300 only, 1.33x native at one row) with fla chunk_kda for KDA prefill; vision tower uses flash_attention_2. No sparse/DSA indexer — the model has none.

interactive.throughput_basis_note: 2026-09-19: output_tokens_per_s_per_gpu is now the METHODOLOGY §4 decode-only rate 111 / 0.0499 s / 8 GPUs = 278.06. The previous 198.9 is b300.md §4.2's SUSTAINED request-cycle rate (batch / (TTFT + OSL x TPOT) x OSL, batch-wave TTFT 10,139 ms) and is kept in sustained_output_tokens_per_s_per_gpu. 2026-09-19 cross-check: Wafer's published B300 measurement (TP8+DCP8, SGLang, DSpark, ISL 1024 / OSL 400, peak at c64, 2026-07-31) gives 196 peak-aggregate out tok/s/GPU — within 1.5% of the 198.9 sustained figure, corroborating the sustained basis and leaving the 1.42x/2.91x gap to 278.06/569.4 fully explained by the decode-only basis (see b300.md §3.8); no number changed.

pairs.headline: Kimi-K3's reference platform: fits one 8xB300 node at 195 GB/GPU, runs the native MXFP4 checkpoint at W4A8, TP8+DCP8. S1 $7.39-14.99/1M out decode-only ($10.34-20.95 sustained; blended $2.38-4.83), S4 $3.61-7.32. Beats the Moonshot API at Hyperstack's $7.40/GPU-h; loses to it at OCI's $15.00 for interactive traffic.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
pairs.parallelism: TP8 + DCP8 per 8-GPU replica (2 NVL4 trays, inside the 72-GPU NVLink domain); 9 independent replicas per NVL72 rack. Wide-EP alternatives DEP16 (210 GB/rank, 16 GPUs) and TEP8/TEP16 are validated but measure below 8-GPU replicas on per-GPU throughput; PP8xTP1 is the prefill-optimal shape. 4 GPUs (one tray, 1,152 GB) does not fit the 1,560.9 GB checkpoint.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 native (W4A8, FlashInfer trtllm-gen SiTU on the sm_103 block-scaled tcgen05 datapath) for the routed experts; non-expert tensors BF16 as shipped; FP8 KV. No dequant and no requant path. nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4 also runs natively but measured slower than MXFP4 without speculation on the sibling B300.
pairs.attention_kernel: TOKENSPEED_MLA (10.x-only, force-requires FP8 KV) for the 24 gated-MLA layers, alternates FLASHINFER_MLA / TRTLLM_RAGGED / cutedsl_mla; FlashInfer fused_kda_decode for the 69 KDA linear-attention layers - its gate is literally compute_capability in ((10,0),(10,3)), i.e. B200 and B300/GB300 only, measured 1.33x the vLLM native fused kernel at one row (geomean 1.13x); MoonViT-V2 asks for FA2. FlashMLA is NOT available (SM90/SM100 only, sm_103 unlisted); this model has no DSA sparse indexer.
pairs.headline: Runs natively on GB300 - MXFP4 W4A8 + FP8 KV, min 8 GPUs (2 NVL4 trays), TP8+DCP8, 9 replicas/rack; TP past 8 buys only +6% (measured). $19.74/1M out interactive, $14.52 max-throughput at OCI's $18/GPU-h, the only published rate - beats Moonshot's API only above ~50% utilisation.

contradictions: GB300 per-GPU TDP: research/gpus/gb300.md (§1.1, §8.1) states 1.4 kW, while research/cross-cutting/cloud-pricing.md (§8.1) states 1,100 W (citing Lenovo's GB300 NVL72 product guide verbatim). The audited document (kimik3/gb300.md §4.1) already surfaces this itself and does not silently pick one; the $2.569/GPU-h colo-amortised anchor it derives is unaffected since it uses the rack-level 135 kW figure, not per-GPU TDP. Flagged here per instructions, not newly discovered.

pairs.gpu: NVIDIA A100 SXM 80GB (HGX 8-GPU; no FP8/FP4 tensor cores)
pairs.parallelism: TP32 across 4 HGX A100 nodes (attn-TP 32), multi-node over 200 Gb/s IB. No EP>8, no DP-attention, no DCP on sm_80; MLA KV stays TP-replicated. Minimum fit is TP32 (4 nodes): 24 is not a legal TP size (7168 ∤ 24; gcd(96, 7168) = 32) and is not in METHODOLOGY §3's topology set {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 72}.
pairs.weight_format_used: MXFP4 experts stay packed in HBM and dequantise in-kernel via Marlin W4A16 (memory win, zero compute win); 57.19 B non-expert params run native BF16. No engine publishes this path on sm_80 and vLLM #35922 reports the Marlin MoE FP4 path crashing on A100 — contested, see doc §6.1.

AITER's tuned ASM hd256 kernel (aiter#5403, still an open PR) is MHA-only, so Marlin falls back to CK. Fused gfx950 GDN prefill (aiter#5606, 2.1-3.8x) is also unmerged.

pairs.headline: Fits 58x over on one MI355X (4.43 GB of 259 GB usable), but no engine registers MarlinForConditionalGeneration and the --hf-overrides fix has never been run on ROCm. BF16 executes, so the 10.1 PF FP4 path is unreachable. Prefill-bound: ~$1.16 per 1,000 two-minute captions at OCI's $8.60.
